title: SD: system suite — test/system/tap1-openrouter.test.js fails on clean main (not host-related, cause unknown)
description:
## Problem

`test/system/tap1-openrouter.test.js` fails under `npm run test:system`: the tap-1 OpenRouter system test. The run never materializes a terminal run with a `loopId` (assertion `a terminal run (loopId) materialized`, `test/system/tap1-openrouter.test.js:58`).

## Why it matters

It is the system witness for the tap-1 path; while it is red it cannot tell a real break from the standing one. The system suite is also the only place these behaviours are exercised end to end, and nothing automated watches it.

## Reproduces on

Repo: **JKershaw/simple-dispatcher**. `npm run test:system` (not in CI; `ci.yml` runs only `npm test`), with `HARBOUR_DIR` pointing at a LinearViewer checkout. Measured by LIN-4181 (merged as PR #309, `11a1279`) on the runner host:

* identical on clean `main` (`0992f39`) and on the LIN-4181 head, run from a workspace clone, a checkout in `/private/tmp`, and a checkout with `TMPDIR` inside `state/`;
* identical against Harbour `9e397e6b`, `10b2c82f` and `0dc1620e`;
* each also fails when its file is run on its own.
  So it is **not** host or location noise, **not** Harbour-version skew and **not** a LIN-4181 regression. The cause is **not known**: LIN-4181 triaged it only far enough to rule those out.

## Acceptance

* The cause is found and stated on this ticket: a real Simple Dispatcher defect, a real Harbour defect (then a Harbour ticket exists), or drift between the test and Harbour.
* `test/system/tap1-openrouter.test.js` passes against the Harbour checkout it is run with, **or** is skipped with a stated, checked reason. It is not loosened to pass: the assertion on line 58 keeps guarding what it guards.
* `npm run test:system` no longer lists `tap1-openrouter` among its failures, run from a workspace clone, with the other three named failures treated separately.

## Anchors

* `test/system/tap1-openrouter.test.js:58`
* `test/system/harness/harbour.js` (how Harbour is started), `test/system/README.md`
* Related: LIN-2471 (an earlier, different red case in the same suite), LIN-4181 (found this; the triage is in its review comments and close-out)

## Unvalidated idea

None worth stating: the cause is unknown. A first step is to run this file alone with Harbour's logs kept and look at what the queue/feed holds at the failing assertion.

---

*Priority: priorityLevel 2 (Medium): no control path involved, cause unknown, suite not in CI. Label: Bug (the workspace catalog has no narrower type label).*

comments.body: Seen again during LIN-4220's review (PR #318, merged as 52d2c3d): this test ("generating a run summary drives Harbour's real OpenRouter client to the fake") still fails under `npm run test:system` on clean main @ 502901c and on the PR head, with the same name on both, against Harbour eb44eff9. Not a regression from #318. Recorded as a further data point.

LIN-4222 (PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/320, merged as 3330526) found this test failing identically on `main` @ `90bbf82` and on its own head: the same failure as named here, with the same pinned LinearViewer checkout (`eb44eff9`). It is not caused by the port change. Run alone it fails the same way. Linked as related; no new ticket filed. LIN-4224's scripted baseline should list this test as known-red until this ticket closes.

Fixed by the same lookup change as LIN-4187 (PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/324). Cause confirmed: the poll looked only in `feed.recent`, so the run finished within the day in `active` and the loop timed out on `a terminal run (loopId) materialized`. Run alone before the change: that assertion failed. After the change: `tap1-openrouter` passes, including the run-summary call reaching the wire-fake, so no further cause is left to record. Close once PR #324 merges and clean-main baseline shows it green.

## Close-out — LIN-4188

Fixed and verified on clean main.

* **Cause:** drift, same as LIN-4187. Harbour LIN-3983 (`d3f67854`) moved the Sessions feed to a 24h recency rule, so a run that finished within the day is in `active`; `tap1-openrouter.test.js` polled `feed.recent` only and timed out on `a terminal run (loopId) materialized`.
* **Fix:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/simple-dispatcher/pull/324 (merged as `d8d186c`): the test now finds the session through the shared `findSession` helper over `active ∪ recent`.
* **Evidence, post-merge, clean `main` @ `d8d186c`, Harbour `d7ceb373`:** `npm run test:baseline -- --tier system` → 127 tests, 127 pass, 0 fail; `test/system/tap1-openrouter.test.js › generating a run summary drives Harbour's real OpenRouter client to the fake (not the mock)` is `pass`, so the run-summary call reaches the wire-fake and no further cause remains. No known-red line printed (`KNOWN_RED` is now empty).
